info.title: Square Cloud API
info.description: Public REST API for the Square Cloud platform.

tags.name: Account
tags.description: The authenticated user's account: profile, plan, owned resources and personal snapshots.

tags.name: Lifecycle
tags.description: Application lifecycle and runtime: create, delete, info, status, logs, metrics, actions, realtime.

tags.name: File Manager
tags.description: Read, upload, rename and delete files in a running application's filesystem.

tags.name: Environment Variables
tags.description: Manage the application's environment variables (read, merge, replace, remove).

tags.name: Network
tags.description: Custom domains, edge cache, DNS configuration and traffic analytics.

tags.name: Deployments
tags.description: Manual and Git-based deploy pipelines, GitHub App installation, commit uploads, deploy history.

tags.name: Snapshots
tags.description: Create, restore, list and download application snapshots.

tags.name: DB Lifecycle
tags.description: Database lifecycle and runtime: create, delete, info, status, metrics, start/stop, update.

tags.name: Credentials
tags.description: Rotate database access password and read the TLS certificate.

tags.name: Database Snapshots
tags.description: Create, restore and list database snapshots.

tags.name: Workspaces
tags.description: Multi-user collaboration: workspaces, members, app sharing and role-based permissions.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: Public webhook receivers (Git providers). Authenticated by route-specific signatures.

tags.name: AI
tags.description: OpenAI-compatible chat completions served by Square Cloud's hosted model. Authenticate with your account API key; point any OpenAI SDK's baseURL at /v2/ai.

ErrorCode.description: Machine-readable error code. The list grows over time: treat a code you do not know as a generic failure of the HTTP status it came with.

code.description: Machine-readable code. New codes may be added: handle an unknown one by its HTTP status.

cpu.description: CPU usage. Formatted (`"0.5%"`) by default, or a number with `?rawData=true`.

ram.description: RAM in use (the allocated memory is not included). Formatted in MB (`"120.4MB"`) by default, or a number of MB with `?rawData=true`.

storage.description: Storage usage. Formatted by default, or raw bytes with `?rawData=true`.

network.description: Network counters. Strings by default (`"<incoming> ↑ <outgoing> ↓"`); two-element `[in, out]` integer arrays with `?rawData=true`.

uptime.description: Unix timestamp (ms) at which the resource last started. `null` when not running.

cpu.description: CPU usage as `"0.00%"`. Present only when `running` is `true`.

ram.description: RAM usage as `"0.00MB"`. Present only when `running` is `true`.

key.description: Signed query string used to compose the snapshot download URL.

version_id.description: Storage version of this snapshot. Pass it as `versionId` to the restore routes.

url.description: Signed download URL, valid for 30 days.

runtime.description: What the archive holds: the database engine (`mongo`, `mysql`, `postgres`, `redis`) or the app language (`javascript`, `typescript`, `python`, ...). `null` on snapshots taken before this field existed.

origin.description: `automatic` for the daily scheduled snapshot, `manual` when a user (or the AI agent) requested it. `null` on snapshots taken before this field existed.

EnvVars.description: Environment variables as an arbitrary `{ key: value }` map of strings.

desc.description: Optional free-form description. Key is omitted when not set.

owner.description: User identifier of the application owner.

cluster.description: Cluster identifier the application is hosted on.

domain.description: Default `<subdomain>.squareweb.app` hostname. Key is omitted for apps without one.

custom.description: Custom domain bound to the app. Key is omitted when not configured.

desc.description: Optional. Key is omitted when not set.

lang.description: Runtime language, the same value as `App.language` (e.g. `javascript`).

desc.description: Free-form description. Present but `null` when unset.

lang.description: Runtime language, the same value as `App.language` (e.g. `javascript`).

owner.description: User identifier of the database owner.

cluster.description: Cluster identifier the database is hosted on.

port.description: TCP port the database listens on.

password.description: One-time database password. Shown only at creation; cannot be recovered.

certificate.description: Base64-encoded PEM (private key followed by the certificate) for TLS connections. `null` when it could not be produced at creation.

connection_url.description: Ready-to-use connection string with the password embedded.

memory.description: Live memory accounting for the user across all applications and databases. All values are in MB.

limit.description: Total memory budget granted by the plan.

used.description: Memory currently allocated to applications and databases.

duration.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds at which the current plan expires. `null` for plans that never expire (e.g. `free`).

name.description: Display name of the member; null when it cannot be resolved (e.g. a deleted account).

group.description: Permission tier. `owner` and `admin` have full management; `maintain` adds operational access (commit, app actions, files, DNS, cache); `manager` covers monitoring and lifecycle control; `view` is read-only.

joinedAt.description: Server-set timestamp of when the member joined the workspace. Not accepted as input. For the owner, equals the workspace creation time.

id.description: Workspace identifier: a UUID v4 with hyphens stripped (32 hex chars). Older workspaces keep a 40-hex id.

owner.description: User identifier of the workspace owner.

referers.description: Referer breakdown. Empty referer strings are normalized to `type: "Direct"`.

providers.description: ASN breakdown. Square Cloud's own ASN is normalized to `type: "SQUARE-CLOUD-PLATFORM"`.

ips.description: Top client IPs by request count over the whole window. IPs originating from Square Cloud's own network are masked (`X.X.XXX.XXX`).

status_codes.description: Edge response status codes over the whole window (all classes, not just errors).

bots.description: Verified-bot categories over the whole window. Traffic without a verified bot category is `type: "Unverified"`.

content_types.description: Response content types over the whole window. Unknown content types are `type: "Unknown"`.

buckets.description: Map of HTTP status code (as string) to request count.

by_status.description: Map of HTTP status code (as string) to request count for this (method, path).
Map of HTTP status code (as string) to request count for this HTTP method.
Flat per-status breakdown. Note: this is an ARRAY of `{ status, requests }`, unlike the nested `by_status` maps inside `top_paths` and `by_method`.

name.description: File or directory name (no path component).

lastModified.description: Last-modified time as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds; may carry a fractional part. `null` when the entry could not be read.

type.description: Record type. `txt` covers both ownership and SSL validation; `cname` is the traffic record.

name.description: Record name to set at the DNS provider.

value.description: Record value. For `cname`, this is always `cname.squareweb.app`.

status.description: Upstream validation state (e.g. `pending`, `pending_validation`, `active`). Passed through from the edge provider.

id.description: Deploy identifier: the commit SHA (40 hex).

state.description: Lifecycle stage. `pending` queued, `clone` Git checkout, `commit` file diff snapshot, `restarting` container restart, `success` finished, `error` failed (see `code` / `message`).

source.description: Always `git`: only Git deploys (webhook and GitHub App pushes) are recorded.

code.description: Present on `state: "error"` events: why the deploy failed (e.g. `AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED`, `INVALID_BRANCH`, `CLONE_FAILED`).

message.description: Present on some `state: "error"` events: the failure details.

files.description: Present on `state: "commit"` events. Lists the files changed in this deploy.

InvalidJsonBody.description: The request body could not be parsed as JSON.

value.message: This API key does not have the scope required by this route.
This API key is restricted to a set of resources that does not cover this request.

RateLimitedEndpoint.description: The caller hit this endpoint's own cooldown.

DatabaseUnavailable.description: The platform database is temporarily unavailable. Retry in a few seconds.

example.message: The database is temporarily unavailable. Please retry in a few seconds.

apiKey.name: Authorization
apiKey.description: User API token or JWT session token. Length 64-1024 chars. A key restricted to scopes reaches only the operations whose `x-scope` it holds; an operation without `x-scope` needs a full-access key.

post.summary: Create a chat completion
post.description:
OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint. Point any OpenAI SDK at baseURL `https://api.squarecloud.app/v2/ai` using your account API key, and call `chat.completions.create`.

Available on Standard, Pro and Enterprise plans. Each plan bounds requests per day, concurrency, pacing between requests and context/output size (Standard: 1,000 requests/day, 16k in / 4k out, 1 concurrent, 5s between requests. Pro: 5,000 requests/day, 24k / 6k, 1 concurrent, 2s. Enterprise: unlimited requests, 32k / 8k, 2 concurrent, no delay). Token usage is billed against your plan's daily AI budget, and each plan also has a daily fair-use allowance on the gateway sized for moderate use (Enterprise gets 5x the base allowance; both reset 00:00 UTC).

The model has a built-in `web_search` it can trigger on its own for current or external information; searches run server-side and only the final answer is returned. You may also declare your own `tools` (OpenAI function-calling format): the model's calls to them come back as a standard `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` response, and you send the results back as `role: "tool"` messages.

Streaming is not supported yet. Error responses use the OpenAI error shape (`{ error: { message, type, code } }`).

messages.description: Chat history: objects with `role` (system | user | assistant | tool) and string `content`. Assistant messages may carry `tool_calls`; tool messages need `tool_call_id`.

tool_calls.description: On assistant messages: the tool calls being answered.

tools.description: Your own tools, in the OpenAI function-calling format: { type: "function", function: { name, description, parameters } }.

max_tokens.description: Completion token cap; silently clamped to your plan's output ceiling.

stream.description: Must be false/omitted (streaming not supported yet).

200.description: The completion, in the OpenAI chat.completion shape. When the model calls one of YOUR tools, `finish_reason` is `tool_calls` and the message carries `tool_calls` instead of text.

message.content: Hello! How can I help you today?

400.description: Malformed body (`invalid_json_body`, `invalid_messages`, `invalid_tools`, `invalid_tool_choice`), unsupported feature (`stream_not_supported`), or the prompt exceeds your plan's context ceiling.

error.message: Streaming is not supported yet on this endpoint. Send stream: false (or omit it).

401.description: The API key was not recognized (`access_denied`).

error.message: This credential was not recognized. An API key stops working the moment it is revoked, regenerated or expires — check the one in your account settings. A session token may simply have expired, in which case sign in again.

403.description: The account's plan does not include the public AI API (Standard and up, `upgrade_required`), the API key lacks the `ai:chat` scope (`missing_scope`), or the key is restricted to resources (`resource_not_allowed`).

error.message: The Square Cloud AI API is available on Standard, Pro and Enterprise plans. Upgrade at https://squarecloud.app/pricing.

413.description: The request body is larger than this endpoint accepts (`payload_too_large`).

error.message: The request body is too large.

429.description: Plan pacing or fair use: a request is already in flight (concurrent_limit_reached), the per-request delay has not elapsed (rate_limit_exceeded), the plan's daily request ceiling is reached (daily_request_limit_reached, resets 00:00 UTC), the plan's daily fair-use allowance on the gateway is reached (daily_spend_limit_reached, resets 00:00 UTC), or the daily AI token budget is spent (daily_limit_reached, resets 00:00 UTC). `rate_limited` is the account's global API budget.

error.message: You are sending requests too quickly for your plan. Wait for the per-request delay and try again.

503.description: All model capacity is busy; retry shortly (`server_overloaded`). `daily_capacity_reached` means the gateway's shared daily capacity is used up; it resets at 00:00 UTC. `database_unavailable`: the platform database is briefly unavailable, retry in a few seconds.

error.message: The model is currently overloaded. Please retry shortly.

post.summary: Create a new application from an uploaded zip
post.description:
Accepts a `multipart/form-data` upload containing a single zip archive and starts the application. The response payload depends on the application language.

The caller must have at least 256 MB of available memory on their plan. Rate limited to 1 upload every 3 seconds per user.

file.description: Zip archive containing the application source.

200.description: Upload accepted and the application provisioned. `description` and `domain` are present only when set in `squarecloud.config`; `language` is the detected runtime with version; `ram`/`cpu` are the allocated resources.

description.description: Optional description (from `DESCRIPTION` in `squarecloud.config`). Omitted when unset.

domain.description: Full `<subdomain>.squareweb.app` host (from `SUBDOMAIN` in `squarecloud.config`). Omitted for non-web apps.

cluster.description: Cluster the application was deployed to.

version.description: `VERSION` from `squarecloud.config`, lowercased: `recommended` or a pinned version (e.g. `22`, `3.12`).

400.description: The upload was rejected by validation or storage.

value.message: Upload failed due to a third-party error. Please try again later.

413.description: Upload exceeded the 100 MB per-file limit.

503.description: Application provisioning is temporarily unavailable due to maintenance. `DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE` is also possible while the platform database is unavailable.

get.summary: List every domain configured across the account's applications
get.description:
Returns a flat list of every hostname configured across the applications owned by the caller: the default `<subdomain>.squareweb.app` hostname (`type: "subdomain"`) and any attached custom domain (`type: "custom"`). Custom domains are listed first, followed by the default subdomains. Applications without a web domain are omitted.

Served from the cached project list, so it does not count against the per-application network rate limits. Rate limited to 20 requests per 60s per user.

200.description: Flat list of configured domains. Empty array when the account has no web applications.

app_id.description: 32-char hex identifier of the application the domain belongs to.

type.description: `subdomain` for the default `*.squareweb.app` hostname, `custom` for an attached custom domain.

get.summary: List the account's custom-domain load balancers
get.description:
Groups the caller's applications by attached custom domain. Every custom domain appears as one group with the applications serving it; a group with two or more applications is an active load balancer (traffic is balanced across them at the edge, with automatic failover when an application is offline).

`limit` is how many applications may share one domain on the caller's plan: 2 on Standard, 5 on Pro, 10 on Enterprise.

Served from the cached project list. Rate limited to 20 requests per 60s per user.

200.description: The plan's per-domain `limit` and the custom domains grouped by hostname; `balancers` is empty when no application has a custom domain.

limit.description: Maximum applications allowed on one domain for the caller's plan.

get.summary: List runtime stats for every application
get.description:
Returns live runtime stats (CPU, RAM, network, uptime) for every application owned by the caller, or scoped to the workspace passed via `workspaceId`.

Rate limited to 15 requests per 60s per user.

parameters.name: workspaceId
parameters.description: Limit the listing to applications shared in this workspace.

200.description: Compact runtime stats for every application in the requested scope.

404.description: Application or workspace not found.

delete.description:
Removes the application, releases any custom domain, and invalidates the caller's project and workspace caches. The operation is rejected while a snapshot restore is in progress.

Rate limited to 1 request every 3 seconds per user.

parameters.name: appId
parameters.description: Application identifier. Optionally suffixed with -<workspaceId> to act on a workspace-shared application.

403.description: A snapshot restore is currently running for this application. An API key can also get `MISSING_SCOPE` (lacks this operation's scope) or `RESOURCE_NOT_ALLOWED` (restricted to other resources).

example.message: A restore operation is currently in progress for this app.

404.description: Application not found or the delete operation failed.

get.summary: Get application information
get.description: Returns the application's identity, plan, region, language, and DNS configuration. The response is scoped to the caller; access to workspace-shared applications is granted automatically when the caller is a member of the owning workspace.

parameters.name: appId
parameters.description: Application identifier. Optionally suffixed with -<workspaceId> to act on a workspace-shared application.

post.summary: Upload a file or zip to an application as a commit
post.description:
Streams a `multipart/form-data` file to the application. A `.zip` is unpacked at the destination; other files are placed at `path/name`. The optional `path` query parameter controls the destination directory inside the application.

File names that look like path traversal, control characters, or `.`/`..` are rejected. Content-Type is derived server-side from the extension.

Requires the workspace Maintainer or Administrator role (or ownership) when called against a workspace-shared application. Rate limits: 1 commit per 2s per user (global) and 1 commit per 5s per (user, application).

parameters.name: appId
parameters.description: Application identifier. Optionally suffixed with -<workspaceId> to act on a workspace-shared application.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Destination directory inside the application (no traversal, no shell metacharacters).

400.description: The upload was rejected by validation or storage.

value.message: Upload failed due to a third-party error. Please try again later.

413.description: Upload exceeded the 100 MB per-file limit.

delete.summary: Unlink the GitHub App repository from an application
delete.description:
Removes the GitHub App repository linkage created via `POST /v2/apps/:appId/deploy/github-app`. Returns 400 if no GitHub App link is configured.

Rate limited to 3 calls per 60s per user.

parameters.name: appId
parameters.description: Application identifier. Optionally suffixed with -<workspaceId> to act on a workspace-shared application.

400.description: The application has no GitHub App repository configured.

404.description: The application does not exist or is not owned by the caller.

post.summary: Link a GitHub repository via the Square Cloud GitHub App
post.description:
Associates the application with a GitHub repository + branch installed through the Square Cloud GitHub App. The branch must be ≤256 chars and the (repository, branch) pair must not already be linked to another application (of any account).

The caller's GitHub account must be connected, the repository must belong to a GitHub App installation that account holds (otherwise `403 REPOSITORY_NOT_AVAILABLE`), and the account must have write access to it (otherwise `403 REPOSITORY_PERMISSION_REQUIRED`). Rate limited to 3 calls per 60s per user.

parameters.name: appId
parameters.description: Application identifier. Optionally suffixed with -<workspaceId> to act on a workspace-shared application.

200.description: Repository linked. `full_name` is the canonical `owner/name` GitHub reports, whatever case or form was sent.

400.description: The request failed validation or the application already has a Git repository configured.

value.message: repositoryName and repositoryBranch are required
Branch name is too long. Max 256 characters

403.description: The account has no usable GitHub connection, the repository is not covered by a Square Cloud GitHub App installation the caller's GitHub account holds, or that account lacks write access to it. An API key can also get `MISSING_SCOPE` (lacks this operation's scope) or `RESOURCE_NOT_ALLOWED` (restricted to other resources).

value.message: Connect (or reconnect) your GitHub account to link a repository.
Repository Installation Required.
Write access to this repository is required.

404.description: The application does not exist or is not owned by the caller, or the repository was not found.

409.description: Another application (of any account) already links the same (repository, branch) pair; its id is only echoed to its owner.

Failed to validate repository

Failed to validate repository

post.summary: Configure or remove the Git deploy webhook
post.description:
Configures the application to deploy on push from a Git provider. Passing `access_token: "@"` removes the webhook; passing a GitHub personal access token (`ghp_*` / `github_pat_*`) enrolls the application and returns its webhook URL.

Requires the workspace Administrator role (or ownership) when called against a workspace-shared application. Rate limited to 5 calls per 60s per user.

parameters.name: appId
parameters.description: Application identifier. Optionally suffixed with -<workspaceId> to act on a workspace-shared application.

access_token.description: GitHub personal access token (`ghp_*` / `github_pat_*`), or `@` to remove the existing webhook.

response.description: Present when configuring; absent when removing.

400.description: `access_token` does not match the accepted format.

get.summary: List recent deploys for an application
get.description: Returns the deploy log for the application as a 2-D array: each inner array is one deploy's lifecycle (`pending` → `clone` → `commit` → `restarting` → `success`). A failed deploy ends in an `error` event carrying `code` (and `message` when there are details). Only Git deploys (webhook or GitHub App push) are recorded, so `source` is always `git`. Empty array when no deploys have been recorded.

parameters.name: appId
parameters.description: Application identifier. Optionally suffixed with -<workspaceId> to act on a workspace-shared application.

200.description: Recent deploys grouped by deploy attempt.

response.description: One inner array per deploy attempt.

items.description: Lifecycle events for a single deploy, in chronological order.

get.summary: Get current Git deploy configuration
get.description:
Returns the GitHub App repository linkage and the deploy webhook URL configured for the application. The response is cached for 5 minutes per (owner, application).

Requires the workspace Manager or Administrator role (or ownership) when called against a workspace-shared application.

parameters.name: appId
parameters.description: Application identifier. Optionally suffixed with -<workspaceId> to act on a workspace-shared application.

200.description: Current Git deploy configuration. Either `app` (GitHub App), `webhook`, or both may be present.

app.description: GitHub App repository linkage. When present, normally has all three fields populated. To detect a missing linkage, check whether `app` is omitted from the response.

delete.description:
Removes the given keys from the application's environment variables. Unknown keys are silently ignored.

Requires the workspace Administrator role (or ownership) when called against a workspace-shared application.

parameters.name: appId
parameters.description: Application identifier. Optionally suffixed with -<workspaceId> to act on a workspace-shared application.

400.description: The request failed validation or the environment variables could not be persisted.

value.message: Static apps do not support environment variables.

get.description:
Returns the application's environment variables as a `{ key: value }` JSON object. Static applications do not support environment variables and return 400.

Requires the workspace Administrator role (or ownership) when called against a workspace-shared application.

parameters.name: appId
parameters.description: Application identifier. Optionally suffixed with -<workspaceId> to act on a workspace-shared application.

200.description: Environment variables as a `{ key: value }` map.

400.description: The application is static, or the environment variables could not be loaded.

post.summary: Merge new environment variables into the existing set
post.description:
Adds or updates environment variables. Existing variables not present in the request body are preserved. Up to 256 variables per application; each key max 1024 chars; each value max 4096 chars.

Requires the workspace Administrator role (or ownership) when called against a workspace-shared application.

parameters.name: appId
parameters.description: Application identifier. Optionally suffixed with -<workspaceId> to act on a workspace-shared application.

envs.description: Variables to merge into the existing set.

400.description: The request failed validation or the environment variables could not be persisted.

value.message: Static apps do not support environment variables.
You can only have up to 256 environment variables.

put.summary: Replace the entire set of environment variables
put.description:
Replaces the application's environment variables with exactly the set provided in the request body. Variables not listed are removed; pass an empty object to wipe all of them.

Limits: up to 256 variables, each key max 1024 chars, each value max 4096 chars.

Requires the workspace Administrator role (or ownership) when called against a workspace-shared application.

parameters.name: appId
parameters.description: Application identifier. Optionally suffixed with -<workspaceId> to act on a workspace-shared application.

envs.description: Complete env set. Replaces all existing variables.

400.description: The request failed validation or the environment variables could not be persisted.

value.message: Static apps do not support environment variables.
You can only have up to 256 environment variables.

delete.summary: Delete a file from an application
delete.description:
Removes the file at the given `path`.

Requires the workspace Maintainer or Administrator role (or ownership) when called against a workspace-shared application.

parameters.name: appId
parameters.description: Application identifier. Optionally suffixed with -<workspaceId> to act on a workspace-shared application.

path.description: Absolute path of the file to delete.

400.description: Path validation failed or the file could not be deleted.

get.summary: List files in an application directory
get.description:
Lists files and directories at the requested `path`. Defaults to the application root when no `path` is given.

Requires the workspace Maintainer or Administrator role (or ownership) when called against a workspace-shared application.

parameters.name: appId
parameters.description: Application identifier. Optionally suffixed with -<workspaceId> to act on a workspace-shared application.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Directory inside the application to list. Defaults to `/`.

400.description: Path validation failed, or the path is not a readable directory.

403.description: The path is inside a directory the file manager does not expose. A workspace member whose role does not allow this gets `PERMISSION_DENIED`. An API key can also get `MISSING_SCOPE` (lacks this operation's scope) or `RESOURCE_NOT_ALLOWED` (restricted to other resources).

404.description: The directory does not exist.

patch.summary: Rename or move a file within an application
patch.description:
Renames the file at `path` to `to`. Both paths must be valid and distinct.

Requires the workspace Maintainer or Administrator role (or ownership) when called against a workspace-shared application.

parameters.name: appId
parameters.description: Application identifier. Optionally suffixed with -<workspaceId> to act on a workspace-shared application.

path.description: Absolute path of the source file.

to.description: Absolute path of the destination file.

400.description: Path validation failed or the rename operation failed.

put.summary: Create or replace a file in an application
put.description:
Writes the provided content to the given path, at most 10 MB. For binary files send `content` base64-encoded with `encoding: "base64"`; a UTF-8 string, a byte array or a `{ type: "Buffer", data }` object are also accepted. Empty content writes an empty file. Writes to `squarecloud.app` / `squarecloud.config` are parsed as platform config (display name, description, memory, autorestart, subdomain) and trigger plan/quota validation.

Requires the workspace Maintainer or Administrator role (or ownership) when called against a workspace-shared application. Rate limited to 10 writes per 5 seconds per user; config rewrites are additionally limited to 1 request every 15 seconds per user.

parameters.name: appId
parameters.description: Application identifier. Optionally suffixed with -<workspaceId> to act on a workspace-shared application.

path.description: Absolute path to write inside the application.

oneOf.description: File content as a UTF-8 string (for text files), or base64 with `encoding: "base64"`. An empty string writes an empty file.
File bytes as integers in [0, 255]; an empty array writes an empty file.
File content as a JSON-encoded byte array (for binary files).

content.description: File content. Accepts a UTF-8 string, a base64 string (with `encoding: "base64"`), a byte array, or a `{ type: "Buffer", data: number[] }` object.

encoding.description: Set to `base64` when `content` is the file base64-encoded (recommended for binary files).

400.description: The path or content failed validation, or a parsed config field was rejected.

403.description: The write was blocked by the workspace's permission settings. A workspace member whose role does not allow this gets `PERMISSION_DENIED`. An API key can also get `MISSING_SCOPE` (lacks this operation's scope) or `RESOURCE_NOT_ALLOWED` (restricted to other resources).

example.message: This route is blocked based on your workspace settings permissions.

get.summary: Open a Server-Sent Events stream of realtime application events
get.description:
Opens an SSE connection that streams the application's realtime feed (deploy progress, status changes, live metrics, log lines) for up to 10 minutes per connection. Each user is limited to 5 concurrent realtime connections, and each application to 30 across all users.

The stream emits these event types:

- `event: system` carries protocol-level signals; the `data:` line is a single uppercase code: `REALTIME_CONNECTING | <sseId>` on connect, then any of `REALTIME_TIMEOUT`, `REALTIME_DISCONNECTED`, `REALTIME_RECONNECT`, `REALTIME_ERROR`.
- `event: logs` is a single log line whose FIRST character is a stream-id byte: `\u0001` (stdout) or `\u0002` (stderr). Read `data.charCodeAt(0)` (1 = stdout, 2 = stderr), then `data.slice(1)` for the line text. A line without that prefix byte is stdout.
- `event: status` carries live container metrics as a JSON string, about one frame per second. The FIRST frame of each (re)connection is COMPLETE: `{ cpu, cpuLimit, ram: [usedMB, limitMB], status, netIO: { i, o, new: { i, o } }, bIO: { i, o }, uptime }` (`cpuLimit` is the number of CPU cores allocated; `uptime` is StartedAt as epoch ms; `netIO.new` is bytes per second). Every later frame is LEAN, carrying only the live fields `{ cpu, ram, netIO, bIO }`: the run-constant fields (`cpuLimit`, `status`, `uptime`) are omitted, so MERGE each lean frame onto the last full frame and keep the previous values for the missing fields. While this stream is open, prefer it over polling `GET /v2/apps/:appId/status`, which can be up to about a minute stale for an application with an open realtime stream.
- `event: error` carries an error code such as `CONTAINER_NOT_FOUND`.

Shapes vary by event, so parse structured payloads (the `status` JSON and most `system`/app messages) defensively and merge successive `status` frames.

parameters.name: appId
parameters.description: Application identifier. Optionally suffixed with -<workspaceId> to act on a workspace-shared application.

200.description: SSE stream established. Content type is `text/event-stream`.

logs.description: One log line. First character `\u0001` = stdout, `\u0002` = stderr; no prefix = stdout.

status.description: Container metrics as JSON. The first frame per connection is complete, later frames carry only `cpu`, `ram`, `netIO`, `bIO`: merge them onto the last full frame.

event: system
data: REALTIME_CONNECTING | abc123-1716000000000-deadbeef

event: status
data: {"cpu":12.5,"cpuLimit":1,"ram":[128,512],"status":"running","netIO":{"i":2048,"o":4096,"new":{"i":64,"o":128}},"bIO":{"i":0,"o":0},"uptime":1716000000000}

event: status
data: {"cpu":13.1,"ram":[131,512],"netIO":{"i":2176,"o":4288,"new":{"i":72,"o":140}},"bIO":{"i":0,"o":0}}

event: logs
data: \u0001Server listening on :3000

event: logs
data: \u0002Error: connect ECONNREFUSED

Otherwise the route answers `202 SNAPSHOT_PROCESSING` while it keeps generating in the background — expected for large databases, not a failure. Poll the snapshot listing (`GET /v2/databases/:databaseId/snapshots`) ~2min later instead of re-posting.

Rate limits: 1 snapshot per 5s per user, 1 snapshot per 3min per database, and the plan's daily snapshot quota per user.

parameters.description: Database identifier.

post.summary: Receive a Git provider push webhook
post.description:
Public endpoint that receives a `push` event from a Git provider (typically GitHub). The webhook token in the URL path (`:webhook`) authenticates the call; no Authorization header is sent.

Accepts `application/json` only. The optional `branch` query parameter filters which branch triggers a deploy — if present and `body.ref` does not match `refs/heads/<branch>`, the request is accepted with 202 but no deploy is queued. The optional `restart` query parameter (`?restart=false`) skips the post-deploy application restart.

Responses are `text/plain` and always say whether a deploy was queued; only the 429 of the rate limit is the JSON error body. A 200 is sent only after the deploy job is stored: on a temporary failure the answer is 503 and the push must be redelivered. Rate limited to 1 push per 15 seconds per webhook token.

parameters.name: webhook
parameters.description: Per-application Git webhook token (64 hex chars).

parameters.name: branch
parameters.description: Lowercase branch name (≤256 chars). When provided, only matching pushes trigger a deploy.

parameters.name: restart
parameters.description: Pass `false` to skip the post-deploy application restart.

200.description: The deploy was queued. It is only answered after the job is stored.

text/plain.example: Deploy queued: commit 1a2b3c4 of 'main' will be deployed shortly.

202.description: Received but not queued: the pushed branch does not match the webhook's `branch`.

text/plain.example: Push received but not queued: it is for 'dev', and this webhook only deploys 'main'. Nothing was deployed.

400.description: The webhook URL or the payload is invalid. Nothing was queued.

invalid_id.value: Invalid webhook URL: the webhook ID is missing or malformed. Nothing was deployed.

json.value: Invalid JSON payload. Nothing was deployed.

no_repository.value: Missing repository data in the payload. Nothing was deployed.

no_owner.value: Missing repository owner data in the payload. Nothing was deployed.

no_ref.value: Missing 'ref' in the payload: expected a 'push' event, got 'ping'. Nothing was deployed.

branch_long.value: The branch parameter is too long (max 256 characters). Nothing was deployed.

404.description: The webhook ID is not linked to any application. Nothing was queued.

text/plain.example: Unknown webhook: it is not linked to any application (it may have been regenerated). Nothing was deployed.

413.description: The payload is larger than 25MB. Nothing was queued.

text/plain.example: Payload too large (max 25MB). Nothing was deployed.

415.description: Content-Type is not `application/json`. Nothing was queued.

text/plain.example: Unsupported Content-Type: set the webhook to send application/json. Nothing was deployed.

503.description: The push was valid but could not be queued (temporary failure). Nothing was deployed: redeliver it from the provider or push again. `DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE` is also possible while the platform database is unavailable.

text/plain.example: Push received but NOT queued: a temporary failure on our side kept the deploy from being stored. Nothing was deployed. Redeliver this webhook (GitHub: Settings > Webhooks > Recent Deliveries) or push again.

get.summary: Get the aggregate platform and dependency status
get.description:
Square Cloud's overall status, the health of each Square Cloud service, and the current status of the external providers the platform depends on.

`status` on each entry is one of `operational`, `degraded`, `outage`, `maintenance` or `unknown`. **`unknown` means the check could not be verified and is NOT evidence of an outage** (some providers publish no status API, so their health is read from a page marker; a page redesign reads as `unknown` rather than as a false alarm).

`summary` is present **only when an entry is not operational**, where it explains what is wrong and what it affects. A healthy entry carries no summary, because the status already says it.

Only Square Cloud's own services influence the top-level `status`: a third-party incident is reported under `dependencies` without flipping the platform badge. Entries are ordered by blast radius.

Served from a document refreshed every 5 minutes; `stale: true` means that document was unavailable and the payload was probed live instead.

200.description: Current status. `status`/`message` describe Square Cloud itself, `services` are Square-run, `dependencies` are third parties.

status.description: `unknown` means the check itself could not run; it is not evidence of an outage.

summary.description: What is wrong and what it affects. Present only when not operational.
